subject: Non-tender (MLB)
query: what does non-tender mean in baseball
title: What does non-tender mean in baseball? MLB deadline is Nov. 20
answer: To non-tender a player means an MLB team declines to offer him a contract for next season, so he becomes a free agent at once. It mostly happens to arbitration-eligible players whose next salary would be higher than the team wants to pay. The 2026 non-tender deadline is 4 p.m. Central on Nov. 20.
body:
Players with fewer than six years in the majors are still under team control. Each winter the team must "tender" them a contract by the deadline to keep them. Those eligible for salary arbitration can get large raises on their second, third and fourth trips through the process, so a club may let a useful but costly player go rather than risk an arbitrator's number. Teams also non-tender players with injury questions, or to free a spot on the 40-man roster. Non-tendered players skip waivers, can sign with any team, and sometimes return to their old club on a cheaper deal.

This year the deadline carries extra weight. The labor agreement between owners and players expires at 11:59 p.m. Eastern on Dec. 1, 2026, and owners are widely expected to lock players out the next day. During a lockout, major league transactions freeze, so players cut on Nov. 20 would have only about 11 days to sign before the market could stop.
in_the_news: MLB's 2026 non-tender deadline falls on Nov. 20, less than two weeks before the labor agreement expires on Dec. 1.

faq.q: When is the 2026 MLB non-tender deadline?
faq.a: 4 p.m. Central (5 p.m. Eastern) on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026.

faq.q: Is a non-tendered player a free agent?
faq.a: Yes. He becomes a free agent immediately, without going through waivers, and can sign with any team, including his old one.

faq.q: What does tender mean in MLB?
faq.a: To tender is to offer a contract for next season to a player still under team control, usually one eligible for salary arbitration.
